sentences: offset = S1[4:0] and width = S2[4:0]: the bits above are ignored, so an offset of 36 reads as 4 and a width of 32 as 0 (a width of 0 gives 0).
When offset + width > 32 the field stops at bit 31, as for `s_bfe`: width = min(width, 32 - offset), and `v_bfe_i32` sign-extends from bit 31.
Example: `v_bfe_i32` of `0xd2f90159` with offset 28 and width 16 gives `0xfffffffd` (4-bit field `0xd`), not `0xd`, and `0x80000000` with offset 31 and width 4 gives `0xffffffff`.
The translator (`bfe_width` for VGPR or SGPR offset and width, the same cut folded at translation time for constants) already did this.

Source: **measured on RDNA2**, AMD Radeon 610M (`gfx1036`, Windows 11, AMD driver 32.0.11016.14003), wave32 and wave64 identical, 16 words over VGPR, inline-constant and literal operands: `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both --group valu_bfe_past31`, 4/4 cases match the translator.
The words are pinned on the CPU by `tests/test_int_hw_probe.py` (`ValuBfeMeasuredOnRdna2`).
